core_obligations: Say X = Spec(A), T = V(f_1, ..., f_r); the case r = 0 (T = X) follows from pseudo-coherence on affines and the definitions.
Let t be the top degree with H^t(E) nonzero; induct on t (base t < m trivial).

H^t(E) is of finite type; its finitely many generators s are realized by maps K_e[-t] -> E via the carded representation lemma; summing gives P -> E with P perfect supported on T, H^i(P) = 0 for i > t, H^t(P) -> H^t(E) surjective.
In the triangle P -> E -> E' -> P[1], E' is m-pseudo-coherent, H^i(E') = 0 for i >= t, and the support condition on the lower cohomology sheaves persists.
Inductively approximate E'; assemble P -> P'' -> P' -> P[1] and extend to a map of triangles by TR3; P'' is perfect and supported on T.
The diagram chase shows P'' -> E is an approximation of (T, E, m).
proof_roadmap: Affine setup; induction on top degree; Koszul representation of generators; triangle reduction; inductive assembly with TR3; approximation check.
difficulty_reason: An induction-on-cohomological-degree engine driving an explicit approximation construction with a TR3 assembly; the content is genuine.
